learning_outcomes.text: Be able to identify simple mechanisms in real systems to efficiently approach their study.

Know how to calculate velocities and accelerations of the different parts of mechanisms; for this, they must know how to apply vector theorems to mechanical systems and interpret the results obtained.
Understand and apply the concepts of center of mass and inertia to mechanical systems.
Know how to perform an analysis of the forces and moments acting on mechanisms to represent them and understand their operation as well as the interaction between different elements.
Know the energetic equations and know how to apply them to mechanical systems.
Be able to perform a simple vibration analysis.
Know the English vocabulary related to the subject.

syllabus_topics: Inclined planes. Wedge. Screw. Basic mechanisms
Module II. KINEMATICS AND PLANE DYNAMICS
Topic 4. PLANE KINEMATICS OF RIGID BODIES
Rigid bodies and types of motion
General movements: velocities. Relative velocity. Angular velocity
General movements: accelerations. Relative acceleration. Angular acceleration
Topic 6. PLANE DYNAMICS OF RIGID BODIES
Energy and Work: Principle of conservation of energy
Kinematic and dynamic analysis of a crank-connecting rod mechanism. Instantaneous Center of Rotation (CIR)
Kinematic and dynamic analysis of a cam. Inclined plane
Study of the Inertia of different bodies. Steiner's Theorem
Reading on technological applications of mechanisms and simple machines
Complementary problems with statements in English
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (lectures) with audiovisual aids, blackboard explanations, and problem-solving
Display and development of theoretical conceptual schemes on each topic
Explanation and resolution of typical problems on the blackboard
Use of videos showing mechanism operation and tutorials for static and dynamic analysis
Technical English practice through specific readings
Practical classes in the classroom (problem-solving sessions)
Revision of individual work during classroom practicals
Resolution of doubts on the blackboard and provision of solutions
Reading of practice guidelines and clarification of doubts before experiments
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a learning support tool (for contrasting methods, verifying results, expanding knowledge)

assessment_methods.method: Activities proposed in the Virtual Classroom (submission of at least three mechanics problems solved with Octave)
Prior knowledge test (on vector mathematics and basic physical concepts)
Free body diagram of simple mechanisms (wedge, pulleys, lever, etc.) test
Kinematics of a point, calculation of centers of mass, and application of Steiner's Theorem test
Plane kinematics and dynamics, Energy and Vibrations test (including an English vocabulary question)

assessment_rules: The course can be passed through continuous evaluation or a single evaluation. Laboratory practices are mandatory for all students, and an 'APTO' (Pass) grade is essential to pass the course. For continuous evaluation, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for the final test (P2.4), and at least 50% correctly solved for other development tests (P2.1, P2.2, P2.3), and 100% for Virtual Classroom activities (P1.1). If minimum requirements for continuous evaluation are not met, the final grade will be 3.5 out of 10 (fail). For the single evaluation mode, a final test accounts for 100% of the grade, with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 on the first part required for the second part to be corrected. Failed practices require taking a development test with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to pass them.
